security_privacy_cost_impact: No new role, credential, policy or client grant. app.jobs gains four columns that hold identifiers (a user id or a system actor's name, a request id, a correlation id), each bounded to 1-128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._:-], so an e-mail address, a phone number with spaces or free text cannot be stored there; the shape is NOT a PII control, since a digits-only phone number, a 13-digit citizen-ID shape and a dotted personal name fit it (A1-174-2, measured by A1; open_blockers[202] (5)); and the actor is bound by shape alone, not to a user or a member of the workspace, which the first enqueue path must add before the worker's audit actor is trusted (A1-174-1, D14); no client role can read them (050: no client grant on app.jobs), and app_worker may SELECT and INSERT them but no role may UPDATE them. Rules 10 and 11 close two reaches A1 measured open since 173 gave app_worker a login (CREATE on the database; EXECUTE beyond PUBLIC's, which also caught an anon EXECUTE in app no other probe saw). No secret or customer data in any file; fixture ids are synthetic. Cost: two more catalog reads per migrate-clean (about 1 s).
migration_and_data_impact: One forward migration, 174_job_tenant_context.sql: four NOT NULL columns and four CHECKs on app.jobs, two column grants to app_worker, four comments, one apply-time block. No data change: app.jobs holds no row wherever 174 applies, and on a populated table the ADD fails closed (23502, measured). No earlier apply-time block superseded (post-migrate 55/39/16). The snapshot declares 174 not applied to the provisioned instance (it alters 050's table, which the instance has never received).
compatibility_impact: Tests 691 -> 692 (one in foundation-contract): floor 85 -> 86 and name digest moved in scripts/test-suite-contract.mjs, evidence/VERIFICATION.md written by the record script. Three probe digests move (pinned check, pinned grant, vocabulary check), each with its reason. rls-smoke cases unchanged (1200); authz proofs 13 -> 14 discharged (one NOT RUN on a trust cluster, unchanged). Every writer of app.jobs must now name the four columns; the three in the repository do. RFC-2026-026's worker half must read them. Review round (fb62e17): tests unchanged (692); the pinned check probe digest moves again, 3ba8cd283ac50444 to 792a2204f6d7a5da (its correlation drift re-bounded to {1,255}, Q0 F3), with its reason; the static writer test reads any spelling of insert into app.jobs (C0-174-4); 174's statements unchanged (a header comment added, A1-174-2).
known_limitations: CTR-JOB-001's reading of tenant_context is not restated and the narrowing of CTR-TEN-001's three ids is not in the contract: contract-catalog/ is read-only here (open_blockers[202] (2)).
174 is declared not applied to the provisioned instance (open_blockers[202] (3)); rules 10 and 11, like rules 2-4 and 7-9, fail by design there until Q170-c.

Rule 10 does not read TEMPORARY or CONNECT without grant option (PUBLIC's defaults); rule 11 reads EXECUTE beyond what PUBLIC holds only; a pg_catalog EXECUTE grant is refused first by the system object fingerprint (measured), so rule 11's pg_catalog reach is a second line.
174's block reads 171 (6)'s predicate, so it shares what open_blockers[198] (6) says that predicate does not see.
The proof's UPDATE control updates zero rows (no policy admits app_worker), so the UPDATE rule is held by 174's block and the pinned grant probe's column rule, not by a row moved.
try-it's demo ran on 55479, not 5507, because the tool refuses 5507 by design (disposition D10).

The job's actor is bound by shape alone: actor_kind and actor_id are checked independently, and a uuid that is no user is admitted (A1-174-1); owed to the batch that writes the first enqueue path (D14, open_blockers[202] (5)).
The identifier shape is not a PII control: digits-only phone numbers, 13-digit citizen-ID shapes and dotted personal names fit it (A1-174-2).

That the isolation enqueue names the four columns is held by the static writer test alone: with RLS on, row level security refuses before NOT NULL, and CI's negative control for app.jobs is satisfied by service-sees-zero-job-rows either way (Q0 F1, D12; the CI change is offered to the Integration Owner).
Rule 11's names are regprocedure text; they are stable because the probe's one executor pins search_path = pg_catalog (D13, measured); a second executor would have to pin it too.

INFO limits stated on open_blockers[202] (5): the proof compares SQLSTATE only (C0-174-3); NULL is set on correlation_id alone and a one-column default is read by 174's block alone (Q0 F2); the WS:905 writer is held statically and by a harness CI does not run (Q0 F4).
